title: Histograms and distribution: choosing the bin

videos.script: Four hundred deliveries. How long does a Horta delivery take? {{question}} The average is thirty-five minutes. But that one number hides everything a manager needs. Are most deliveries close to thirty-five? Are some taking an hour? {{average}} A histogram answers that. It cuts the range of times into intervals, counts the deliveries in each, and draws a bar for every count. {{cut}} Here it is with intervals of five minutes. One peak, around half an hour. And a long tail to the right. A few deliveries took more than an hour. {{five}} Now watch what happens when the interval changes. Two minutes: ragged spikes, mostly noise. Fifteen minutes: seven blocks, and the tail has vanished. {{change}} The data never moved. Only one setting did. The bin width. {{bin}} This lesson is about choosing it, about the rules that suggest a first guess, and about the views that need no bins at all. {{plan}}
